page.layout: One page of running text in one column; marginal notes in the right margin (section number "6." and the note "Fame excitatur desiderium futuræ vitæ.") beside the second paragraph. Running head at the top, page number 48 at the top right.

main_text.p: versis domat nostram carnem, & cristas contundit. Docet nos quibus indigeamus, & quam necessaria nobis sit gratia ipsius. Vniuersum genus hominum si omnes suas vires coniungeret, & artes adhiberet, non possent vel culmum producere, vel vuam[?] creare, interim tam insolenter se gerunt, ac si non omnia ex liberalitate Dei acciperent. Deo subtrahente manu, res nostrae non aliter habent, quàm liberorum, quos primum incedere, aut illorum quos natare docemus, quum primum manum ab eis retrahimus, illi concidunt in terram, hi verò in fundum mergun-tur. Hæc tamen ante non expendimus quam Deus cruce nos exerceat.

Præterea6. Deus fame aliisq; his ærumnis in suis fidelibus futuræ vitæ desiderium accendit & contemptum huius ærumnosæ vi-ta docet, ut tandem ad meliorem aspirent. Nam si ex animi nostri sententia omnia succederent, nemo hinc migrare & mundum deserere vellet, de altera & meliori vita parum solliciti essemus. page.notes: Right margin: the section number "6." and the marginal note "Fame excitatur desiderium futuræ vitæ." are both attached to the paragraph beginning "Præterea"; they are placed at the start of that paragraph in the transcription. Uncertain reading: "vuam" in "vel vuam creare" (probably "quam"), marked [?]. The third paragraph breaks off at the foot of the page at "su-" and continues on the next page; the fragment is kept as printed.
